rules.rule: Declare the property class of every screw and nut; do not design to 12.9 strength when commodity 8.8 / A2-70 will be bought
rules.criterion: each fastener SKU carries a class (8.8, 10.9, 12.9, A2-70); ratings use that class's proof load
rules.severity: warning: catalogue proof loads are class 12.9 while the SKU names no class
rules.auto: catalogue field; compare required preload with the class

rules.rule: Size the screw to the joint: preload must exceed the working load with margin; prefer a longer clamp length
rules.criterion: 0.75 x proof load x n >= 2 x separating load; clamped length >= 3 d where vibration matters (longer bolts keep preload after embedding)
rules.severity: info: few printer joints are strength-limited
rules.where: AGENT.md: 'Bolt preload and contact' not checked
rules.auto: joint force from FEA reactions / load cases against n x preload

rules.rule: Minimum thread engagement by tapped material
rules.criterion: steel >= 1.0 d; aluminium >= 2.0 d (Nord-Lock; Tameson 2.0-2.5 d; mechloop uses 1.5 d); brass / cast iron 1.5-2.0 d; plastic >= 2 d or use an insert; a standard nut = full strength
rules.applies: screws into tapped holes; T-nuts and catalogue tapped holes exempt
rules.where: interference: thread_engagement, thread_bottoms_out (1 d steel, 1.5 d aluminium, 2 d plastic)
rules.auto: already; consider 2 d for aluminium and 1.5 d for brass
rules.note: SOURCES DISAGREE on aluminium: 1.5 d (mechloop, common shop rule) vs 2 d (Nord-Lock) vs 2-2.5 d (Tameson)

rules.rule: Do not thread deeper than the thread can use
rules.criterion: engagement <= 3 d

rules.rule: Blind tapped holes need run-out below the thread; the screw must not bottom
rules.criterion: unthreaded depth >= 1.5 d below the last full thread (taps under M6); screw tip >= 1 pitch short of the bottom
rules.severity: error if the screw bottoms (no clamp), warning for run-out

rules.rule: Use a threaded insert or a nut where a soft material is assembled repeatedly
rules.criterion: plastic or soft aluminium + a screw that is removed in service (wear part, cover) => insert or through-bolt with nut
rules.auto: threads_into plastic and screw on a declared service item

rules.rule: Clearance holes to ISO 273; choose the class deliberately
rules.criterion: fine / medium / coarse: M2.5 2.7/2.9/3.1, M3 3.2/3.4/3.6, M4 4.3/4.5/4.8, M5 5.3/5.5/5.8, M6 6.4/6.6/7.0, M8 8.4/9.0/10.0; larger than coarse needs a washer (FST-031); patterns of 4+ screws or printed parts: medium or coarse
rules.severity: info (class), warning (under fine, or over coarse without a washer)
rules.where: tolerance: pattern start (p_all_start); parts.clearance_hole() gives one 'close' value, unverified
rules.auto: measure each hole around each screw (tools/practice_audit.py does)

rules.rule: Keep the pressure under the head and the nut below what the clamped material can carry
rules.criterion: preload / bearing area <= limiting surface pressure (use yield of the clamped part if no figure); bearing area = pi/4 (dw^2 - dh^2)
rules.auto: preload from class torque, area from head and measured hole
rules.note: limit values per material are recalled / assumed

rules.rule: Plain washer under any head or nut that sits on a slot, an oversize hole, a soft or painted surface
rules.criterion: slot or hole > ISO 273 coarse, or head face supported < 80 % => ISO 7089 washer (M3 3.2x7x0.5, M4 4.3x9x0.8, M5 5.3x10x1.0); large slots: ISO 7093 wide series
rules.applies: slots, oversize holes, printed and thin parts
rules.severity: warning: head digs in, adjustment creeps, joint loosens
rules.auto: supported fraction of the head annulus on the first clamped part

rules.rule: Washer under the element that is turned on aluminium (anodised or bare) and on coated parts
rules.criterion: nut or head rotated against aluminium / paint => washer, to keep friction repeatable and the coating intact
rules.auto: material of the bearing part + which end is turned (the one with tool access)

rules.rule: Countersinks only in sheet thick enough to keep a cylindrical land
rules.criterion: sheet >= 3.18 mm for a countersink (SendCutSend); head height <= 60 % of t (recalled)

rules.rule: Leave enough floor under a counterbored head
rules.criterion: floor under the head >= 0.6 d in aluminium (recalled); check FST-030 on the floor
rules.where: manufacture: cnc floor / wall minimums (0.5-0.8 mm only)
rules.auto: thickness of the first clamped interval when the head is recessed

rules.rule: State a tightening torque for every structural joint; derive it from class, friction and the weakest clamped material
rules.criterion: reference: 90 % of yield at mu 0.14 (Bossard F.047 basis); class 8.8 about M3 1.3, M4 2.9, M5 5.7 N.m (recalled); reduce to the FST-030 limit on soft parts
rules.auto: generate a torque table per screw group into BUILD.md

rules.rule: Do not design a joint that only works at an exact preload
rules.criterion: hand torque scatter +/-35 % (feel), +/-25 % (torque wrench): a joint must work between 0.65 and 1.35 of nominal preload
rules.auto: could bracket friction-joint checks (STR-014) with 0.65x preload

rules.rule: Edge distance and pitch of fastener holes
rules.criterion: hole centre to edge: nominal 2 d, minimum 1.5 d; pitch nominal 4 d
rules.applies: metal parts; plastics want more (>= 2 d, recalled)
rules.where: manufacture: sheet.hole_to_edge_t_ratio (1 t of web: a cutting rule, not a strength rule), fdm.thread_wall_d_ratio
rules.auto: distance from each screw axis to the nearest boundary of each clamped part

rules.rule: A joint needs two fasteners, or one fastener plus a feature that stops rotation
rules.criterion: parts joined by one screw must also share a pin, key, shoulder, rib-in-slot or a second screw
rules.severity: warning: the part swings on its screw under vibration
rules.auto: screws per part pair; then look for a second contact that blocks rotation about the screw axis (or a declared join)

rules.rule: Do not carry a sustained or alternating shear load on screw friction through clearance holes or slots when a shoulder, pin or hook can carry it
rules.criterion: service load across a slotted / clearance joint <= mu (0.15) x preload x 0.65 / 2; otherwise add a positive stop (jack screw, pin)
rules.applies: belt tension anchors, motor mounts on slots, sliding mounts
rules.severity: warning: slip is what loosens screws
rules.auto: belt tension and declared loads against friction capacity of the screws in slots; credit a jack screw that touches the part

rules.rule: Nuts and tapped parts must sit on the threaded part of a partially threaded screw; the plain shank must be shorter than the grip
rules.criterion: ISO 4762 thread length b = 2 d + 12 (M3 18, M4 20, M5 22, M6 24 mm); screws up to about M3x20, M4x25, M5x25, M6x30 are threaded to the head; every nut / tapped interval must start >= (L - b) below the head
rules.applies: long cap screws, studs made from screws
rules.severity: error: cannot be assembled as drawn
rules.auto: thread zone per screw against each threaded target's interval along the axis
rules.needs: b per size in the catalogue (already in vendor_docs CSV)

rules.rule: Use stocked lengths and sizes
rules.criterion: length in the preferred series (4 5 6 8 10 12 16 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 60 ...) and inside the product standard's range for the diameter (ISO 4762: M3 5-30, M5 8-50); otherwise confirm a supplier
rules.where: interference STANDARD_LENGTHS_MM (used for bottoming only); ratings BOM
rules.auto: table lookup

rules.rule: Thread should show past a nut, but not far
rules.criterion: protrusion >= 1 pitch (2 pitches in aerospace practice, recalled) and <= about 3 d unless it is an adjuster
rules.severity: info / warning (flush or short: nut not fully engaged)
rules.where: interference: nut counted full strength once the screw passes through
rules.auto: tip position against the nut's far face

rules.rule: Threads out of the shear plane
rules.criterion: in a joint loaded in shear the plain shank, not the thread, crosses the interface
rules.applies: shear joints with loads near capacity
rules.auto: needs FST-060 data plus a load; low value for a printer

rules.rule: Every fastener on a vibrating or moving assembly has a declared locking provision
rules.criterion: one of: prevailing-torque nut (nyloc), thread adhesive (medium strength, removable), serrated-flange screw / nut, or a joint shown not to slip (FST-052); plain nut + plain screw alone is not a provision
rules.applies: screws on moving bodies, motors, pulleys, bed, anything that sets an adjustment
rules.severity: warning: a printer vibrates for thousands of hours
rules.auto: per screw: body is moving or a motor is in the joint, and no locking attribute
rules.needs: add_screw(..., locking='nyloc'|'adhesive'|'serrated'|None) and nyloc / serrated catalogue parts

rules.rule: Do not specify split (helical spring) lock washers as a locking device
rules.criterion: no split lock washers in the BOM
rules.auto: BOM scan

rules.rule: Nylon-insert nuts: temperature and reuse limits
rules.criterion: nylon locking element <= about 120 degC (250 degF); replace after a few reassemblies; near the hotend or under the bed use all-metal locknuts or adhesive rated for the temperature
rules.auto: distance to el.hot_parts and the thermal estimate

rules.rule: Thread adhesives (anaerobic) attack some plastics; keep them off ABS, PC, PETG parts
rules.criterion: adhesive locking only where the screw touches metal alone; for screws through plastic use nylocs or serrated flanges
rules.auto: locking='adhesive' and a plastic in the stack

rules.rule: Tooth / star washers scratch the seat: use them for earth bonding, not as a general lock on finished or highly stressed parts
rules.criterion: star washers only at protective-earth points
rules.where: electrical: earth_point product text (ring terminals and star washer)
rules.auto: BOM scan

rules.rule: Standardise fasteners and tools
rules.criterion: target <= 2 thread sizes and <= 3 lengths per size on the main assembly; one drive type; count distinct SKUs and tools and report
rules.where: assemble / score: fastener_types, tool_changes (reported, no threshold)
rules.auto: count; suggest merges (a length only used <= 4 times with a neighbour that fits)

rules.rule: Avoid look-alike fasteners that are not interchangeable in the same area
rules.criterion: two lengths of one size differing by <= 2 mm where the shorter one is needed to avoid bottoming (e.g. M3x6 next to M3x8 into 3.5 mm-deep block threads) => warn, key or segregate
rules.applies: catalogue tapped holes with a maximum depth
rules.severity: warning: the wrong screw jams a guide block or cracks a motor end bell
rules.auto: per sub-assembly: would the next longer SKU in the BOM bottom out here?

rules.rule: Screws driven straight into printed plastic are for one-time, low-load joints
rules.criterion: no machine screw threaded directly into a printed part where the joint is structural or re-opened; use insert, captive nut or through-bolt
rules.where: interference thread_engagement (2 d in plastic); manufacture fdm.thread_wall_d_ratio
rules.auto: threads_into a plastic part

rules.rule: Heat-set inserts: hole, depth and wall
rules.criterion: straight (not tapered) hole to the insert maker's diameter (M3 brass insert: 4.0 mm, test-print 4.0-4.4); blind hole about 1 mm deeper than the insert; wall around the hole >= 0.5 x insert OD (>= 1.6-2.0 mm for M2-M3); no chamfer needed
rules.auto: insert catalogue part with hole / wall data; measure the boss

rules.rule: Put the insert or captive nut on the side where the load pulls it INTO the part
rules.criterion: screw tension must seat the insert / nut against plastic, not draw it out of its hole
rules.auto: insert on the far side of the clamped stack from the screw head = good; same side = pull-out

rules.rule: Captive nut pockets: closed against rotation, open for insertion, with plastic behind the nut
rules.criterion: pocket across flats = nut AF + 0.2 to 0.4 mm; >= 2 mm (or 0.6 d) of plastic between nut face and the clamped interface; nut insertable in the assembled state or retained
rules.where: interference (nut overlap), assemblability (nut has a path in)
rules.auto: measure the pocket around each nut inside a printed part

rules.rule: Say which T-nut: slide-in nuts must be in the slot before the slot end is closed; drop-in / roll-in nuts for anything added later
rules.criterion: each T-nut SKU names its type; a slide-in nut in a slot whose both ends are blocked at that assembly step is an error
rules.severity: error for trapped slide-in nuts, else info
rules.where: T-nuts are BOM lines, not geometry (AGENT.md)
rules.auto: slot ends blocked at the step where the screw is fitted (assembly order exists)

rules.rule: A part on T-nuts wants two of them (or a key in the slot); a single T-nut pivots and slides
rules.criterion: parts held to an extrusion by one T-nut screw need a second constraint; loads along the slot are carried by friction only (FST-052)
rules.auto: T-nut screws per part

rules.rule: Tapped extrusion ends: tap the core hole to depth, deburr, and back the joint with a bracket where it carries moment
rules.criterion: end tap M5 in the 2020 core hole, engagement >= 2 d in 6063; a blind butt joint on one screw also needs an anti-rotation feature (bracket, plate)
rules.where: interference thread_engagement; fea AssemblyCase lower bound
rules.auto: FST-051 on extrusion ends

rules.rule: Mind galvanic pairs where moisture can stand
rules.criterion: indoors dry: stainless or zinc-plated steel in aluminium is accepted; avoid bare carbon steel sheet against aluminium without a finish; give laser-cut mild steel a finish (paint, zinc, oil)
rules.auto: material pairs in contact + declared finish

rules.rule: An earth bond through anodised or painted metal must break the coating
rules.criterion: serrated washer or scraped seat at every protective-earth joint; anodised extrusions are not bonded to each other by their brackets unless shown
rules.severity: error if a PE path relies on anodised contact
rules.auto: PE continuity graph over metal parts with joint conductivity flags

rules.rule: Exact constraint: count what holds each body; make every redundant constraint compliant, floating or adjusted
rules.criterion: per moving body: constraints from guides, screws, nuts = 6 - DOF; each extra one needs a declared float / flexure / adjustment
rules.where: fea.bed_support constraint / z_over_constrained; tolerance two-rail and screw-to-rail checks
rules.auto: generalise the bed-support constraint count to X and Y

rules.rule: Two parallel rails: one is the master against a reference edge, the other is set parallel to it at assembly and then locked
rules.criterion: allowable non-parallelism MGN12: 9 um (ZF / Z0), 5 um (Z1): only reachable by setting the slave rail with the carriage as gauge
rules.where: tolerance: two rails parallel; Adjustment rail_align

rules.rule: A lead screw must not also be a guide: float the nut or the far end
rules.criterion: nut radial float >= 99.7 % misalignment of screw to rails; do not fix both screw ends rigidly AND the nut

rules.rule: Screws clamp, they do not locate: use dowels, shoulders, ribs-in-slots or a tight pattern where position matters
rules.criterion: a position requirement tighter than the hole clearance (M3 medium: +/-0.2 mm) across a screwed joint needs a locating feature or an adjustment
rules.where: tolerance: joint play of screws is simulated; adjustments credited
rules.auto: list joints whose play dominates a failed stack-up and that have no locating feature

rules.rule: Two-pin location: one round hole and one slot aimed at it
rules.criterion: a part located by two pins / tight screws: second feature is a slot along the line of centres, never two tight round holes more than a few d apart
rules.auto: needs pins as parts

rules.rule: Every adjustment has (a) a controlled way to move it, (b) a lock that does not disturb it, (c) tool access in the finished machine
rules.criterion: Adjustment declares mover (jack screw, nut pair, slot by hand), lock (screws, jam nut, adhesive) and is reachable at the assembled pose
rules.severity: warning: an adjustment that drifts or cannot be reached is not one
rules.where: Adjustment has name, kind, range only
rules.auto: Adjustment(lock=[screw names], mover=...): locks must exist, be FST-070-locked, and pass driver access in the FINAL assembly, not only at their own step

rules.rule: Allow thermal growth: one fixed point, the rest free to slide or flex
rules.criterion: alpha dT L (aluminium 23.6e-6: 0.3 mm on 220 mm at 60 K) must be taken by slots / flexures, not by clamped screws
rules.where: fea ThermalCase (bow, gap); AGENT.md 'fixed at one point and free to grow at the others'
rules.auto: bed held at more than one rigid point without a declared flexure

rules.rule: Abbe: keep the working point close to the guide and the drive in line with the mass centre and friction
rules.criterion: offset nozzle-to-rail and belt-to-centre-of-mass as small as layout allows; report the arms
rules.where: twin: toolhead tilt spring from block spacing and nozzle distance; fea.bed_support screw offset
rules.auto: report arms; no threshold

rules.rule: Bearing spacing against overhang (Saint-Venant / 'golden' proportion)
rules.criterion: spacing of guide points along the travel / distance to the load >= 1 (jam risk below), about 1.6 good, 3 ideal; for plain bushings 2:1 minimum
rules.auto: ratio from block positions and tool point

rules.rule: Short, closed structural loop between tool and work
rules.criterion: human review of the path nozzle - gantry - frame - Z - bed

rules.rule: Locate both members of a critical pair from the same part / the same set-up
rules.criterion: shortest chain between two features that must align
rules.where: tolerance: chains; hints 'locate both parts from one part'

rules.rule: Fit by load direction: the ring that sees a rotating load gets the tight fit
rules.criterion: inner ring rotating under a fixed-direction load: shaft j5-k5 (light press), housing H7 (slide); state the fit of both seats
rules.auto: require a declared fit for each ring

rules.rule: A printed bearing seat is a locating pocket, not a press fit that lasts
rules.criterion: bearing in plastic: retain axially by shoulder + cover / screw / circlip; do not count on interference (creep) and expect 0.1-0.3 mm radial play in a 'sliding' printed seat
rules.auto: bearing whose seat part is plastic: BRG-020 on both sides + radial clearance drawn

rules.rule: Retain the locating bearing axially in BOTH directions, on both rings
rules.criterion: each ring of the locating bearing has a shoulder, sleeve, circlip, cover or collar on both faces; the load path for axial force in each direction is drawn
rules.severity: warning (error when a declared axial load has no path)
rules.where: AGENT.md 'axial retention of bearings' not checked
rules.auto: probe the annulus above / below each ring for an abutting part (tools/practice_audit.py does)

rules.rule: One locating bearing per shaft; the other floats
rules.criterion: exactly one bearing constrained axially both ways; the other free on one ring (thermal growth, no fight)
rules.auto: from BRG-020 results per shaft

rules.rule: Axial load on a deep-groove ball bearing stays a fraction of its static rating
rules.criterion: Fa <= 0.5 C0 (<= 0.25 C0 for small / light-series bearings); 608: C0 1370 N -> about 340 N
rules.where: ratings: guide loads against catalogue ratings ('typical')
rules.auto: axial share of the joint load per bearing
rules.note: the 0.5 / 0.25 C0 figures were searched for and not confirmed today

rules.rule: Axial load goes through a shoulder, collar or circlip, not through set-screw friction or a press fit
rules.criterion: every axial load path element is a positive stop; a set-screwed hub in the path is a warning
rules.auto: axial path from nut to frame: joins of kind set_screw / press on it

rules.rule: Set screws bear on a flat (or dimple), two at 90 degrees, and are locked
rules.criterion: hub on a shaft by set screws: flat or spot on the shaft under at least one screw; two screws at 90 deg (Gates stock pulleys: 2 above 16 grooves); thread adhesive
rules.severity: warning: the classic printer failure (layer shift)
rules.where: v8 docstring: 'pulley set screws' not modelled
rules.auto: set_screw joins: does the shaft have a flat (catalogue attribute)?
rules.needs: shaft flat on nema17(); set screw count on gt2_pulley
rules.note: Machine Design (snippet): a flat adds only about 6 % torsional holding power; its value is repeatable seating and no burr locking the hub on

rules.rule: Never seat a set screw or a bearing on a thread
rules.criterion: bearing bores and hub set screws need a plain turned journal; a T8 thread crest is not a journal (undersize, 4 line contacts, set screw ruins the thread)
rules.severity: warning: runout and a hub that cannot hold
rules.auto: bearing or set-screw hub whose shaft part is a lead screw without a 'journal' interface

rules.rule: Keep overhung loads close to the bearing
rules.criterion: belt pull x overhang within the motor's radial limit; pulley as close to the face as possible

rules.rule: Flexible couplings carry torque, not weight or thrust
rules.criterion: no axial load path through an elastomer / helical coupling
rules.auto: BRG-023 path test

rules.rule: At least 6 teeth in mesh on every load-carrying sprocket
rules.criterion: teeth in mesh = wrap/360 x teeth >= 6; for each tooth fewer (minimum 2) the torque rating falls 20 %
rules.severity: warning with the derated rating; error under 2 teeth or when the derated rating is below the load
rules.where: motion: belt_low_wrap, but only for the pulley named in a joint's drive
rules.auto: apply to every non-idler pulley on the path; compare derated rating with the pulley's torque

rules.rule: At least 60 degrees of wrap on every loaded sprocket
rules.criterion: wrap >= 60 deg
rules.auto: route() already returns wraps

rules.rule: Sprockets no smaller than the pitch's minimum
rules.criterion: 2MGT: check zmin in the maker's table (inside idler minimum 12 grooves); MXL: 10 teeth
rules.auto: table

rules.rule: Idler type: tooth side gets a sprocket (or a flat idler >= 40-groove pitch diameter), the back gets a FLAT, uncrowned idler
rules.criterion: backside idler: smooth, uncrowned; inside flat idler OD >= 25.4 mm (2MGT)
rules.severity: warning: teeth on the belt's back wear the backing and make noise
rules.auto: wrap sense of each idler against the belt's tooth side; idler SKU toothed or smooth
rules.needs: smooth idler catalogue part; tooth side on Belt

rules.rule: Idler diameters
rules.criterion: 2MGT: backside idler OD >= 12.7 mm (0.50 in), and at least 30 % larger than the minimum inside sprocket; inside idler >= 12 grooves; SDP/SI: idler diameter must exceed the smallest drive pulley
rules.auto: idler OD from the catalogue
rules.note: Gates' two statements differ: table 9 gives 0.50 in; '30 % larger than the minimum inside sprocket' (12 grooves, 7.6 mm PD) gives about 10 mm. SDP/SI is stricter (larger than the smallest drive pulley).

rules.rule: Idlers and tensioners on the slack side, locked after tensioning; no spring idler on the tight side
rules.criterion: tensioner on the span leaving the driver in the unloaded direction; lock declared (LOC-006)
rules.auto: for a reversing drive both spans are tight in turn: report only

rules.rule: Pulley diameter not smaller than the belt width
rules.criterion: pulley OD >= belt width
rules.auto: catalogue OD against Belt.width

rules.rule: Flanges
rules.criterion: at least one flanged pulley per belt; both flanged when centre distance >= 8 x small pulley diameter or the shafts are vertical; open-ended belts: clamp alignment replaces a flange
rules.auto: flange attribute of catalogue pulleys; axis direction against gravity
rules.needs: flanged flag (pulley solids already have flanges)

rules.rule: Belt tension is set to a number, with adjustment travel to fit and re-tension
rules.criterion: installation tension declared (Gates minimum per width; fixed-centre positioning Ti = 1.0-1.2 Te); centre-distance adjustment >= what fitting over flanges needs
rules.where: ratings: Belt.tension default from Gates; motion: belt_wrong_length against Belt.adjust

rules.rule: Pulleys in one plane, shafts parallel
rules.criterion: in-plane within 0.5 mm as drawn; under tolerance per the tolerance verifier
rules.where: motion: belt_misaligned; tolerance: belts in plane

rules.rule: Open belt ends: clamp enough teeth, positively
rules.criterion: >= 6 teeth held in a toothed clamp or folded-back grip; no reliance on a zip tie alone
rules.auto: needs clamp geometry

rules.rule: Belt drive brackets must be rigid: centre distance must not change under load
rules.criterion: deflection of motor / idler mounts under 2 x tension small against tooth height (0.76 mm for 2 mm pitch): aim < 0.1 mm
rules.auto: auto-generate an AssemblyCase per belt mount

rules.rule: Stay below the screw's critical (whirl) speed
rules.criterion: n <= 0.8 x n_crit; n_crit grows with root diameter / L^2 and end fixity (fixed-free lowest)
rules.severity: info at printer Z speeds (12 mm/s on 2 mm lead = 360 rpm)
rules.auto: formula with catalogue root diameter and declared end fixity

rules.rule: Check the screw as a column when it is in compression
rules.criterion: Euler load with end fixity >= 3 x axial load
rules.auto: formula

rules.rule: Support the driven end of a screw so that it cannot whip or lift; a free far end is acceptable for short Z screws
rules.criterion: driven end: two bearings spaced >= 3 x shaft diameter (or one double-row), retained per BRG-020; free length / diameter reported
rules.auto: bearing spacing on the screw / diameter

rules.rule: Know where backlash goes: gravity-loaded nuts are fine until something lifts the bed
rules.criterion: nut preloaded by weight only: upward force (crash, sticking print removal) must not unseat nut, screw or bearing
rules.auto: BRG-020 in the upward direction covers the mechanical part

rules.rule: A vertical axis must not fall at power-off
rules.criterion: self-locking screw (efficiency < 0.5, i.e. lead angle below the friction angle) or a brake
rules.auto: catalogue efficiency of the screw

rules.rule: Mounting shoulders and corner reliefs to the maker's table
rules.criterion: MGN12: rail-side shoulder H1 <= 1.7 mm with fillet r1 <= 0.3; block-side shoulder H2 <= 4 mm, r2 <= 0.4
rules.auto: geometry of the part beside the rail foot

rules.rule: Mounting surface flat and stiff enough for the rail
rules.criterion: flatness about 0.05 / 200 mm for MG12 (snippet); an extrusion face is not catalogued for straightness
rules.auto: process flatness class of the seat part

rules.rule: Bolt the rail at the maker's pitch; do not leave holes empty on a loaded rail
rules.criterion: every hole (MGNR12: 25 mm pitch, 10 mm end distance) for rated load and accuracy; every second hole only on lightly loaded axes, said explicitly
rules.auto: screws threading through the rail / holes in the rail

rules.rule: Rail and block bolts torqued to the maker's figure
rules.criterion: M3: about 1.9 N.m in iron, 1.0 N.m in aluminium (snippet, row not confirmed for MGN12); block threads 3.5 mm deep: screw length = plate + 3 mm
rules.auto: torque table (FST-040)

rules.rule: A block must never run off its rail; fit end stops, and keep the block on a rail (or its plastic keeper) during assembly
rules.criterion: mechanical stop inside the rail end at both ends of every rail; assembly order never slides a block off
rules.where: motion: guide run-off over mechanical travel
rules.auto: a part that blocks the block within the rail length beyond mechanical travel

rules.rule: Use the rail's reference edge
rules.criterion: master rail's datum edge against a shoulder, pins or a straightedge at assembly

rules.rule: Moment loads: one block is a pivot
rules.criterion: a single block carries roll / pitch / yaw moments on its own rating and stiffness; prefer two blocks or two rails when the load is off the block
rules.where: ratings: guide loads and moments; twin: toolhead tilt

rules.rule: Close and triangulate frames; a rectangle of extrusions with corner cubes racks
rules.criterion: each frame face has a diagonal, a panel or gusseted corners; report racking stiffness
rules.auto: auto racking load case

rules.rule: Carry loads in tension / compression and shear, not bending of thin sections; keep load paths short
rules.criterion: review

rules.rule: Radius loaded inside corners
rules.criterion: inside corner radius >= 0.25 t on loaded sheet and printed parts; machined pockets >= 1/3 depth
rules.where: manufacture: corner radii (for the cutter, not for stress); fea FoS
rules.auto: sharp concave edges on parts in a load case

rules.rule: Friction joints: check slip
rules.criterion: n x 0.65 x preload x mu (0.15 dry steel / aluminium) >= 1.5 x shear load
rules.applies: slotted and T-nut joints carrying load
rules.auto: same as FST-052

rules.rule: Thin sheet brackets: bend a flange or add a return where they carry out-of-plane load
rules.criterion: flat sheet cantilever length / t <= 10 under belt or motor load, else flange / gusset
rules.auto: auto load case per motor mount (BLT-053)

rules.rule: Hole size and web
rules.criterion: hole >= 0.5 t (laser), recommended >= t; hole edge to part edge >= t (Protolabs: >= 3.2 mm above 0.9 mm sheet)

rules.rule: Features clear of bends; flanges long enough; relief at bend ends
rules.criterion: hole to bend >= 2 t + r; flange >= 4 t (Protolabs) / shop table; relief notch where a bend meets an edge
rules.where: manufacture: sheet.flange_min_t_ratio (2 t + r), sheet.hole_to_bend_t_ratio; bend relief NOT checked
rules.auto: bend line ending inside material without a notch
rules.note: flange minimum differs: mechloop 2 t + r, Protolabs 4 t

rules.rule: One bend radius per part, the shop's tooling radius
rules.criterion: all bends same inside radius = shop table
rules.auto: compare radii across bends

rules.rule: Round the outside corners of sheet profiles
rules.criterion: outside profile corners R >= 1 mm (R >= t preferred, R 3 mm on parts handled in service)
rules.severity: warning: sharp points cut hands and cables
rules.auto: convex profile edges parallel to the thickness with no radius

rules.rule: Order the deburr / edge finish; laser and waterjet edges are sharp and carry dross on the exit side
rules.criterion: every sheet part has an edge-finish note (deburr both sides / tumble) and a corrosion finish for mild steel
rules.severity: warning: cut fingers, cut wire insulation
rules.auto: meta edge_break / finish present

rules.rule: Self-fixturing: tab-and-slot or locating ribs so sheet parts find their place
rules.criterion: slot = t + 0.1 to 0.2 mm; review

rules.rule: Pressed-in hardware clear of edges and bends
rules.criterion: PEM-type hardware: centre to edge per the maker's table; not near bends
rules.auto: needs hardware parts

rules.rule: Tapping thin sheet
rules.criterion: tapped sheet >= 1.5 mm and >= 3 pitches of thread (M3 in 1.5 mm, M5 in 2.5 mm); else rivet nut / PEM / nut

rules.rule: Inside corner radius and pocket depth
rules.criterion: radius >= 1/3 depth; depth <= 4 x width

rules.rule: Standard drills and taps; holes no deeper than needed
rules.criterion: standard drill sizes; depth <= 4 d recommended, 10 d typical; threads M6+ preferred, <= 3 d

rules.rule: Wall thickness
rules.criterion: metal >= 0.8 mm (0.5 feasible), plastic >= 1.5 (1.0)

rules.rule: Few set-ups; related features in one set-up
rules.criterion: <= 3-4 set-ups; features that must align share a set-up

rules.rule: Tolerance only what needs it; everything else to a general tolerance
rules.criterion: general tolerance ISO 2768-m (f where needed) stated; tight tolerances listed individually
rules.auto: DOC-011

rules.rule: Break all machined edges
rules.criterion: edge break 0.2-0.5 mm chamfer or radius on all outside edges (ISO 13715 indication), stated on the drawing; chamfer hole entries that take screws or pins
rules.auto: sharp convex edge length per part (tools/practice_audit.py does) or a declared edge note

rules.rule: Orient layers so the load does not peel them
rules.criterion: principal tension not along the build direction
rules.note: v8 checker note 5: it also fires on compression

rules.rule: Holes print small: compensate, and ream or drill the ones that matter
rules.criterion: vertical holes about 0.15-0.4 mm under; critical bores (bearing seats, shafts, pins) get a 'ream / drill after printing' note
rules.auto: bearing / pin / axle bores in printed parts without a finishing note

rules.rule: Chamfer, not fillet, the edges on the build plate
rules.criterion: 45 deg chamfer 0.4-0.6 mm on bed-contact edges of mating faces (elephant's foot)
rules.auto: sharp convex edges lying on the print_up base plane of a part that mates on that face

rules.rule: Small printed pins and bosses are weak: use bought pins
rules.criterion: pins < 5 mm diameter: fillet at the base or replace with a dowel / screw

rules.rule: Overhangs, bridges, horizontal holes
rules.criterion: overhang <= 45 deg; bridges clean to 5 mm; horizontal holes teardrop or <= 10 mm

rules.rule: Enough plastic around holes, inserts and nuts
rules.criterion: wall around a screw hole or insert >= 1 d (>= 2 perimeters + infill anchoring); >= 3 perimeters around bearing seats

rules.rule: Plastic creeps under a clamped screw: spread the load and do not rely on preload
rules.criterion: screw head / nut on printed plastic => washer (ISO 7089, wide series on PETG / PLA) or metal sleeve (compression limiter) through the plastic; sustained bearing pressure <= about 0.3 x yield (recalled); or reduce the torque and lock the screw (FST-070)
rules.applies: every screw through a printed part
rules.severity: warning: joints go slack over weeks, faster when warm
rules.auto: first clamped part under head / nut is plastic and no washer or sleeve part (tools/practice_audit.py does)

rules.rule: Keep sustained load and heat off low-temperature plastics
rules.criterion: part temperature <= HDT - 15 K under load (PLA about 55, PETG about 70, ABS about 95 degC: recalled); motor mounts, bed parts, hotend parts not in PLA
rules.where: electrical thermal estimates (probe); v8 chose PETG / ABS by hand
rules.auto: material table with HDT against el.hot_parts and motor case temperature

rules.rule: Consolidate parts only as far as each still prints without support and in a strong orientation
rules.criterion: report; no threshold

rules.rule: Functional bores print roundest with their axis vertical
rules.criterion: bearing seats and shaft bores: axis along print_up
rules.auto: bore axis against print_up

rules.rule: Tool access for every screw
rules.criterion: driver envelope clear when the screw is fitted
rules.where: assemblability: driver access (at installation step, home pose)

rules.rule: A nut needs a spanner or a trap; someone must hold it
rules.criterion: each loose nut: spanner swing >= 60 deg or socket access, or a captive pocket; else it spins
rules.where: assemblability checks the screw's driver only
rules.auto: clear annular sector around each nut that is not in a pocket

rules.rule: Assemble from one direction, onto a base, with gravity
rules.criterion: report from_below, turns; target zero from-below fasteners on bench sub-assemblies

rules.rule: Poka-yoke: a part that fits two ways will be fitted the wrong way
rules.criterion: hole patterns of non-symmetric parts are not symmetric under 180 deg rotation / mirroring; left / right parts are identical or cannot be swapped
rules.auto: symmetry test of each part's interface pattern against its full shape

rules.rule: Adjustments and their locks reachable in the finished machine
rules.criterion: see LOC-006
rules.auto: driver access test at the final assembly for named screws

rules.rule: Wear and service parts come out without tearing the machine down
rules.criterion: declared service items (nozzle, belts, bed sheet, fans, hotend, board) each have a removal path that disturbs no alignment (rails, belt planes, bed level)
rules.auto: run the disassembly search for each service item on the finished assembly; list what must come off first

rules.rule: Strain relief at both ends of every moving cable; fixed clamp before each connector
rules.criterion: every flexing span is clamped to a part at both ends, then >= 30 mm of slack to the connector; no flexing at a crimp or solder joint
rules.where: subsystems: cable_clamp_in_air; electrical looms (waypoints with clamp=)
rules.auto: last clamp to connector distance

rules.rule: Bend radius of flexing cables and chains
rules.criterion: continuous-flex cable: bend radius >= 7.5-10 x cable OD (maker's figure); loom / chain radius >= largest member's
rules.auto: derive the minimum from the largest wire OD

rules.rule: Cables clear of sharp edges, hot parts and moving parts; grommet or edge trim where a loom crosses sheet
rules.criterion: loom path >= 3 mm from unbroken sheet edges, or the edge is trimmed / the hole grommeted
rules.auto: distance from loom polyline to sharp edges found by MCH-015 / SHT-014

rules.rule: Label connectors, wires and fasteners groups; mark adjustment directions
rules.criterion: review

rules.rule: Protective bonding of every exposed conductive part that can become live
rules.criterion: PE from the inlet to supply case, frame and each separately anodised metal sub-assembly near mains; continuity verified (test current 0.2-10 A, older edition); green-yellow, own terminal
rules.where: electrical: earth wires to supply and earth_point
rules.auto: FST-111 continuity graph

rules.rule: Ferrules on stranded wire in screw terminals; ring terminals under screws; no tinned ends
rules.criterion: each stranded conductor in a screw terminal has a ferrule sized to the wire
rules.where: electrical: connectors / terminals per wire (twin ferrule text)
rules.auto: terminal kind per port

rules.rule: Segregate mains from low voltage; cover live terminals
rules.criterion: mains conductors routed apart from signal looms, double insulation or barrier; finger-safe covers on supply terminals

rules.rule: Derate connectors and wires
rules.criterion: continuous current <= 80 % of connector rating; heater circuits on screw terminals or rated connectors, not signal headers
rules.where: electrical: connector and gauge checks, 80 % limits

rules.rule: No sharp edges or corners where hands or cables go
rules.criterion: all accessible metal edges broken (MCH-015, SHT-013, SHT-014); extrusion cut ends deburred and capped
rules.auto: sum of sharp convex edge length on parts with no edge note

rules.rule: Pinch and crush points of moving axes
rules.criterion: gaps that close between moving and fixed parts: either < 4 mm (finger cannot enter) or > 25 mm at the end of travel (recalled ISO 13854 finger values), or guarded / low force
rules.applies: axes with drive force > about 75 N
rules.auto: closing gaps from the motion sweep with the joint's available force

rules.rule: Hot surfaces marked and out of casual reach
rules.criterion: bare metal above about 60 degC that can be touched: warning label; bed and hotend unavoidable, state it

rules.rule: Guard or enclose belt run-ins that fingers and hair can reach
rules.criterion: review; open-frame printers accept it

rules.rule: Stability: the machine does not tip or walk
rules.criterion: centre of mass projection inside the foot polygon with margin at a 10 deg tilt; feet declared; reaction of the heaviest axis at max accel < static friction
rules.auto: mass properties + feet positions

rules.rule: Liftable by one person, with somewhere to grip
rules.criterion: mass <= about 20-25 kg for a one-person lift; grips that are not the gantry or the bed
rules.auto: threshold on total mass

rules.rule: Edge-break note on every made metal part
rules.criterion: 'break all sharp edges 0.2-0.5' or ISO 13715 symbol; deburr note on sheet DXF orders
rules.auto: field present; written into the part's fabrication sheet

rules.rule: General tolerance block
rules.criterion: ISO 2768-m (or the process class used by the tolerance verifier) stated per part; only tighter features called out
rules.where: tolerance process classes exist but are not exported to a drawing / order sheet

rules.rule: Torque and threadlocker call-outs in the build instructions
rules.criterion: BUILD.md step for each screw group gives torque (FST-040) and locking (FST-070)

rules.rule: Threads, fits and finishes called out
rules.criterion: tapped holes, press / slide fits and surface finish listed per part (a STEP file does not carry them)
rules.where: manufacture knows the threads each screw needs

RP1228.title: NASA Reference Publication 1228, Fastener Design Manual (R. T. Barrett, 1990)

quotes.lockwasher: The lockwasher serves as a spring while the bolt is being tightened. However, the washer is normally flat by the time the bolt is fully torqued. At this time it is equivalent to a solid flat washer, and its locking ability is nonexistent. In summary, a lockwasher of this type is useless for locking.
quotes.preload_accuracy: Preload measuring method / accuracy, percent: Feel (operator's judgment) +/-35; Torque wrench +/-25; Turn of the nut +/-15; Load-indicating washers +/-10; Fastener elongation +/-3 to 5; Strain gages +/-1
quotes.edge_distance: Common design practice is to use a nominal edge distance of 2D from the fastener hole centerline, where D is the fastener diameter. The minimum edge distance should not be less than 1.5D. The nominal distance between fasteners is 4D, but the thickness of the materials being joined can be a significant factor.
quotes.nylon: The main drawback of this pellet is that its maximum operating temperature is approximately 250 F. The nylon pellet will also be damaged quickly by reassembly.
quotes.tooth_washer: Although this washer does provide some locking action, it damages the mating surfaces. These scratches can cause crack formation in highly stressed fasteners, in mating parts, or both
quotes.grip: Standard design practice is to choose a grip length such that the threads are never in bearing (shear). Where an exact grip length is not available, the thickness of the washers used under the nut or bolthead can be varied enough to allow proper grip.
quotes.inserts: An insert is a special type of device that is threaded on its inside diameter and locked with threads or protrusions on its outside diameter [...] such as plastic and nonferrous materials, as well as to repair stripped threads in a tapped hole.
quotes.shear: Whenever possible, bolts in shear should have a higher shear strength than the bearing yield strength of the materials they go through.
quotes.galvanic: The contact of dissimilar materials can create galvanic corrosion, which can become a major problem.
quotes.adhesive: Loctite 242 is for removable fasteners [...] the best adhesives will function at 450 F

BOLTSCI.title: Bolt Science, Self-Loosening of Bolts and Nuts (vibration loosening)

quotes.slip: By far the most frequent cause of loosening is side sliding of the nut or bolt head relative to the joint, resulting in relative motion occurring in the threads. If this does not occur, then the bolts will not loosen, even if the joint is subjected to severe vibration.
quotes.spring_washer: conventional spring lock washers are no longer specified, because it has been shown that they actually aid self loosening rather than prevent it.
quotes.categories: three basic locking fastener categories have been established. They are: free spinning, friction locking, and chemical locking.

GATES.title: Gates, Light Power and Precision Drive Design Manual (PowerGrip GT3 / 2MGT), section 'V. Idler Usage' and belt drive design notes

quotes.teeth: The designer should be sure that at least 6 belt teeth are in mesh on load carrying sprockets. For every tooth in mesh less than this (with a minimum of 2), 20% of the belt torque rating must be subtracted.
quotes.wrap: In order to minimize the potential for belt ratcheting, each loaded sprocket in the system should also have a wrap angle of at least 60 deg. [...] Non-loaded idler sprockets do not have tooth meshing or wrap angle restrictions.
quotes.idler_side: Inside idlers are generally preferred over backside idlers from a belt fatigue standpoint. [...] Inside idlers should be sprockets, but can be flat if the O.D. is equivalent to the pitch diameter of a 40 groove sprocket. Backside idlers should be flat and uncrowned.
quotes.slack: Idlers should be placed on the slack (or non-load carrying) side if possible. [...] If spring loaded idlers are used, they should never be placed on the tight side
quotes.table9: Table 9 - Idler Size Recommendations: 2MGT GT3: minimum inside idler 12 grooves; minimum backside idler 0.50 in O.D.; minimum inside flat idler 1.00 in O.D.
quotes.backside_30: Flat backside idlers should be used with diameters at least 30% larger than the minimum recommended inside sprocket size.
quotes.shear: Proper belt installation tension and rigid drive bracketry and framework is essential in preventing belt tooth jumping under peak torque loads. It is also helpful to design with more than the normal minimum of 6 belt teeth in mesh to ensure adequate belt tooth shear strength.
quotes.set_screws: 12-16 Groove pulleys have 1 set screw, all others have 2 at 90 degrees
quotes.idler_flange: Flanging of idlers is generally not necessary.

SDPSI.title: SDP/SI, Timing Belt Design and Installation Suggestions: General Guide Lines

quotes.teeth: In order to deliver the rated horsepower, a belt must have six or more teeth in mesh with the grooves of the smaller pulley.
quotes.width: The pulley diameter should never be smaller than the width of the belt.
quotes.flange: Because of a slight side thrust of synchronous belts in motion, at least one pulley in the drive must be flanged. When the center distance between the shafts is 8 or more times the diameter of the smaller pulley, or when the drive is operating on vertical shafts, both pulleys should be flanged.
quotes.idlers: Idlers, either of the inside or outside type, are not recommended and should not be used except for power takeoff or functional use. When an idler is necessary, it should be on the slack side of the belt. Inside idlers must be grooved, unless their diameters are greater than an equivalent 40-groove pulley. Flat idlers must not be crowned (use edge flanges). Idler diameters must exceed the smallest diameter drive pulley. Idler arc of contact should be held to a minimum.
quotes.tension: a belt, when installed with a snug fit (that is, not too taut) assures longer life, less bearing wear and quieter operation. Preloading (often the cause of premature failure) is not necessary.
quotes.adjust: provision should be made for some center distance adjustment for ease in installing and removing belts. Do not force belt over flange of pulley.
quotes.frame: A nonrigid frame causes variation in center distance and resulting belt slackness. This, in turn, can lead to jumping of teeth
quotes.align: Be sure that shafts are parallel and pulleys are in alignment.

HUBSCNC.title: Hubs (Protolabs Network), How to design parts for CNC machining

quotes.cavity: Recommended cavity depth: 4 times cavity width
quotes.wall: Recommended: 0.8 mm (metals), 1.5 mm (plastics). Feasible: 0.5 mm (metals), 1.0 mm (plastics)
quotes.thread: The majority of the load applied to a thread is taken by the few first teeth (up to 1.5 times the nominal diameter). Threads longer than 3 times the nominal diameter are thus unnecessary.
quotes.blind: For threads in blind holes cut with taps (i.e. all threads smaller than M6), add an unthreaded length equal to 1.5 times the nominal diameter at the bottom of the hole.
quotes.setups: This is often acceptable if the part needs to be rotated up to three or four times, but anything above this limit is excessive. [...] To achieve maximum relative positional accuracy, two features must be machined in the same setup.
quotes.tolerance: Our tolerances are either 2768 medium or fine. If tolerances are not specified, manufacturing partners will use the selected 2768 grade.
quotes.drawing: you'll have to include a 2D technical drawing if your model includes threaded holes or shafts and/or dimensions with tolerances tighter than the selected 2768 grade.
quotes.drill: Recommended: standard drill bit [...] Holes with a non-standard diameter must be machined with an end mill tool.

HUBSFDM.title: Hubs (Protolabs Network), How to design parts for FDM 3D printing

quotes.holes: FDM often prints undersized vertical-axis holes. [...] If the diameter of the vertical axis hole is critical, the recommendation is to print it undersized and then drill the hole to the correct diameter.
quotes.chamfer: If assembly or overall dimensions are critical to the function of an FDM part, include a 45 deg chamfer or radius on all edges touching the build plate.
quotes.pins: If your design contains pins smaller than 5mm in diameter, add a small fillet at the base of the pin. If function is critical, consider including a hole in your design in the location of the pin, drill the hole to the correct size and insert an off-the-shelf pin.
quotes.overhang: an overhang can usually be printed up to 45 deg without compromising quality
quotes.bridge: sagging or marks from support material are to some extent always present unless the bridge is less than 5mm
quotes.anisotropy: FDM components are inherently weaker in one direction due to layer orientation. [...] the joints between each layer are actually small valleys. This creates a stress concentration with a tendency to crack.

PROTOSHEET.title: Protolabs, Sheet metal fabrication design guidelines

quotes.holes: Holes and slots should be a minimum of material thickness in diameter. If a material is 0.036 in. (0.914mm) or thinner, the hole should be 0.062 in. (1.574mm) from the material edge; if the material is thicker than 0.036 in. (0.914mm), the hole should be at least 0.125 in. (3.175mm) from the material edge to avoid distortion.
quotes.flange: It is recommended to use the same radii across all bends, and flange length must be at least 4 times the material thickness.
quotes.hardware: In situations where hardware inserts are close to bend lines, [...] any hardware hole deformation (due to material stretching in the press brake) may affect the functionality of the insert itself.

quotes.relief: Bend relief notches reduce stress on inner radii and prevent corner tearing or bulging.
quotes.holes: All holes and cutouts are at least 50% material thickness for laser cut parts
quotes.contact: Flanges need to meet the minimum flange length for at least ~50-60% of the bend's length on both sides to provide enough press brake support.
quotes.radius: Bend radius and K factor are set per material thickness. [...] we don't offer custom bend radii.
quotes.deburr: Deburred Mild Steel is more prone to rusting, and is not recommended for outdoor use unless it's coated. [deburring is a separate, optional service: https://sendcutsend.com/services/deburring/]

CNCK.title: CNC Kitchen, Threaded inserts in 3D prints: tips and tricks

quotes.rules: A blind hole should be slightly deeper than the length of the insert (approx. 1 mm). Through holes do not need to be longer than the insert. To ensure strength you should make sure to stick to the minimum wall thickness. Holes should be straight (not tapered). Normally, no chamfer is required at the hole edge.
quotes.why: Each time you screw the parts together, the material gets plastically deformed at the threads, which eventually leaves you with nothing but a ragged hole
quotes.overtighten: If a screw gets turned directly into the plastic and is slightly overtightened, the threads in the plastic will often shear off
